sentences.en: Hello, and welcome to a very special episode of The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收看《历史的其余部分》特别节目。

sentences.en: We are here in the heart of Amsterdam, surrounded by bicycles and trams and thousands of people.
sentences.zh: 我们现在身处阿姆斯特丹的市中心，周围环绕着自行车、有轨电车和成千上万的人。

sentences.en: And we are here, Tom, thanks to WISE, the account that lets you send, spend, and receive money internationally.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们之所以能来到这里，要归功于 WISE，这款能让你在国际间汇款、消费和收款的账户。

sentences.en: Tom, we are going on a Dutch adventure.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们要去开启一场荷兰大冒险了。

sentences.en: We are.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: To learn about the history.
sentences.zh: 去了解这段历史。

sentences.en: Here in the heart of the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 就在荷兰的市中心。

sentences.en: I really hoped that wasn't going to happen, but he has done his Dutch accent.
sentences.zh: 我本来真希望这事不会发生，但他还是秀了他的荷兰口音。

sentences.en: And so we are going on a Dutch adventure to learn about the history of Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们要去开启一场荷兰大冒险，了解阿姆斯特丹的历史。

sentences.en: And Tom, thanks to WISE, we'll be spending like locals.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，多亏了 WISE，我们的消费体验将如同当地人一般。

sentences.en: We will.
sentences.zh: 我们会是的。

sentences.en: So yes, we're here in Amsterdam, and we thought you loved the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们现在在阿姆斯特丹，我们以为你很喜欢荷兰。

sentences.en: You always go on about how you love the Dutch and Dutch history.
sentences.zh: 你总是喋喋不休地说你多么喜欢荷兰人和荷兰历史。

sentences.en: Well, and Holland, obviously.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然还有荷兰（Holland）。

sentences.en: So we thought it would be a fun thing to do, to come to this corner of Northwestern Europe
sentences.zh: 所以我们觉得来西北欧这个角落会是一件很有趣的事，

sentences.en: and to tell the story of the Netherlands through the history of Amsterdam and through a selection of buildings.
sentences.zh: 并通过阿姆斯特丹的历史以及一系列建筑来讲述荷兰的故事。

sentences.en: So you've chosen your favorite historic sites in the city of Amsterdam, and we are going to be exploring the themes of capitalism, of liberalism, globalization, the religious
sentences.zh: 所以你选择了自己在阿姆斯特丹这座城市里最喜欢的历史遗迹，我们将探讨资本主义、自由主义、全球化以及荷兰人宗教宽容的主题，

sentences.en: tolerance of the Dutch.
sentences.zh: 对荷兰人的宗教宽容。

sentences.en: Yeah, because you say that this is an episode about the Netherlands as well as about Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为你说这是一集既关乎荷兰也关乎阿姆斯特丹的节目。

sentences.en: But Dominic, I would go further and say it's a history of the world.
sentences.zh: 但多米尼克，我想更进一步说，这是一部世界史。

sentences.en: Amsterdam is one of those cities that has profoundly shaped the entire course of global history.
sentences.zh: 阿姆斯特丹正是那种深刻塑造了全球历史进程的城市之一。

sentences.en: Well, don't people sometimes say this is the great birthplace or one of the great birthplaces,
sentences.zh: 好吧，人们有时不是会说这是伟大的发源地之一吗，或者是伟大的发源地之一，

sentences.en: along with, I suppose, London, Genoa, Venice, I don't know, of capitalism, of modern international capitalism?
sentences.zh: 我想，除了伦敦、热那亚、威尼斯，还有什么，可以说是资本主义、现代国际资本主义的发源地？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And we will be exploring one of the great kind of shrines to that emergence of capitalism.
sentences.zh: 我们将探索见证资本主义崛起的一处伟大圣地。

sentences.en: But I think of all the cities that have played outsized roles in global history, being one of those places that have altered and changed the course of world history, Amsterdam for
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，在所有对全球历史发挥过超乎寻常的作用、曾改变和重塑世界历史进程的城市中，阿姆斯特丹对我来说，

sentences.en: me is, I think, my favorite because it's the least grandiose.
sentences.zh: 我想，是我最喜欢的一个，因为它是最不宏大的。

sentences.en: It's the least pompous.
sentences.zh: 它是最不自命不凡的。

sentences.en: Dare I say it's perhaps the most comfortable.
sentences.zh: 我敢说它或许也是最舒适的。

sentences.en: And that's a very unusual thing in a kind of world-shaking city to have.
sentences.zh: 对于一座能够撼动世界的城市来说，这是一种非常罕见的特质。

sentences.en: And what makes Amsterdam even more extraordinary is that it seems in some ways so unsuited by geography for its role.
sentences.zh: 而让阿姆斯特丹更加非凡的是，从地理条件来看，它在某种程度上似乎极其不适合扮演这个角色。

sentences.en: So you compared Amsterdam to London as one of the two kind of great birthplaces really of modern capitalism.
sentences.zh: 所以你把阿姆斯特丹比作伦敦，称其为现代资本主义的两个伟大发源地之一。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And London is obviously very well suited by geography to be a great city because it's lowest bridging point on the Thames.
sentences.zh: 伦敦在地理上显然非常适合成为一座伟大城市，因为它是泰晤士河上最低的桥梁渡口。

sentences.en: It's open to the sea.
sentences.zh: 它面向大海开放。

sentences.en: But Amsterdam, the clue is in the name.
sentences.zh: 但阿姆斯特丹，线索就在名字里。

sentences.en: We are currently in Dam Square, which is the kind of ancient heart of the city, because a dam here was built over a river called the Amstel.
sentences.zh: 我们目前身处水坝广场（Dam Square），这里可以说是城市的历史中心，因为当年正是在这里的一条名为阿姆斯特尔河（Amstel）的河流上建造了一座水坝。

sentences.en: But when we call it a river, it wasn't really.
sentences.zh: 但当我们管它叫河时，其实并不太算。

sentences.en: It was really a kind of, it was an extended bog.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是一种，它是一片延伸的沼泽。

sentences.en: And all this area around here, I mean, going back into, you know, the Iron Age, then to the Roman period, early medieval period, it was really just a series of marshes.
sentences.zh: 这里的整个区域，我是说，追溯到铁器时代，然后到罗马时期、中世纪早期，实际上只是一片连绵的泽地。

sentences.en: And we have records, say, from my great friend Pliny the Elder.
sentences.zh: 我们有历史记录，比如说来自我的好朋友老普林尼的记载。

sentences.en: I knew Pliny would come into it somewhere.
sentences.zh: 我就知道普林尼总会在某个地方出场。

sentences.en: So he served up here and he describes seeing people kind of perched on man-made island, things that are called turps, and the seawater's coming in and retreating twice a day.
sentences.zh: 他曾乘船来到这里，他描述看到人们栖息在人工岛上，也就是所谓的“特尔普”（turps）高台，海水每天两次涌来又退去。

sentences.en: And so he says, you know, he asks, are these, you know, is this to be reckoned sea or is it to be reckoned land?
sentences.zh: 所以他说，你知道，他发问，这究竟应该算作海洋，还是应该算作陆地？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's an open question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个悬而未决的问题。

sentences.en: Obviously, the low countries, you know, it's below sea level, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 显然，低地国家，你知道的，它低于海平面，对吧？

sentences.en: And so it's not an obvious place to settle.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是一个显而易见适合定居的地方。

sentences.en: So then why is it that people are settling here?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么人们会选择在这里定居呢？

sentences.en: And the reason is because the soil is unbelievably good.
sentences.zh: 原因是因为这里的土壤好得不可思议。

sentences.en: So you have peat, which is good for farming.
sentences.zh: 这里有泥炭，非常适合耕作。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: But the problem with that is that if you start draining it of water, which, you know, the more you settle here, the more you're doing that.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，如果你开始把水排干，你知道的，你在这里定居得越多，你就是在更多地做这件事。

sentences.en: So it shrinks.
sentences.zh: 所以土地会收缩。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so then you start sinking below the sea level.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会开始下沉到海平面以下。

sentences.en: And Amsterdam is actually, I think, about two meters below the sea.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为阿姆斯特丹大约在海平面以下两米左右。

sentences.en: And then, of course, the danger of flooding becomes even greater.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，发生洪灾的危险就变得更大了。

sentences.en: And the only way that you can combat that danger of flooding is to get together and kind of form a collective and start building dams and dikes.
sentences.zh: 你能对抗这种洪灾危险的唯一方法，就是聚在一起建立一个集体，开始修建水坝和堤防。

sentences.en: Hence, Dam Square.
sentences.zh: 因此有了水坝广场（Dam Square）。

sentences.en: Hence, Dam Square.
sentences.zh: 因此有了水坝广场。

sentences.en: And so Amsterdam is very, it's a very inhospitable geographical position for a city.
sentences.zh: 所以阿姆斯特丹的地理位置非常不适合建立城市。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But the city emerges because the only way you can settle here is to form a collective.
sentences.zh: 但这座城市之所以能够崛起，是因为你在这里定居的唯一方法就是建立一个集体。

sentences.en: And so what basically seems to have happened is that around 1150, 1160, there was really terrible flooding here.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上发生的情况似乎是，在大约1150年到1160年左右，这里发生了非常可怕的洪水。

sentences.en: And so the only way that people could survive was really to start building kind of collective enterprises, dams and so on.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们生存下去的唯一途径就是开始建设某种集体企业，比如水坝等等。

sentences.en: So you have drainage cows start to be dug from the beginning of the 13th century.
sentences.zh: 所以从13世纪初开始，人们就开始开凿排水沟。

sentences.en: And then by about 1250, maybe 1275, people are digging dikes along the banks of the Amstel.
sentences.zh: 然后到1250年左右，也许是1275年，人们开始沿着阿姆斯特尔河岸修筑堤防。

sentences.en: And then they put a dam across it.
sentences.zh: 接着他们在河上横跨筑起了一座水坝。

sentences.en: And where we are now in Dam Square is exactly the spot where they built the dam.
sentences.zh: 我们现在所在的壮观的水坝广场，正是他们当年修建水坝的地点。

sentences.en: So the Amstel back in early Middle Ages was flowing exactly where we are now.
sentences.zh: 所以在中世纪早期，阿姆斯特尔河流经的地方正是我们现在站立的这个位置。

sentences.en: So it's so late by the standards of European capitals, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 以欧洲首都的标准来看，这实在太晚了，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, what are we, 13th century?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们算什么时代，13世纪？

sentences.en: I mean, I suppose Madrid is a late capital, but if you think of so many of the great cities of Europe, Amsterdam is a real parvenu, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，马德里算是一个建都较晚的首都，但如果你想想欧洲那么多伟大的城市，阿姆斯特丹真是一个暴发户，汤姆。

sentences.en: It absolutely is.
sentences.zh: 它绝对是的。

sentences.en: And it remains that pretty much for most of the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 在整个中世纪的大部分时间里，它基本上一直如此。

sentences.en: Its wealth essentially, to begin with, comes from fish.
sentences.zh: 从根本上讲，它最初的财富来自鱼类。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: How glamorous.
sentences.zh: 多有魅力啊。

sentences.en: Well, so herring in particular.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特别是鲱鱼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the Dutch have discovered a particular way of pickling herring that enables it to survive longer and actually makes it tastier.
sentences.zh: 荷兰人发明了一种独特的腌制鲱鱼的方法，能让它保存更长时间，而且实际上让它更美味。

sentences.en: And so they corner that particular market.
sentences.zh: 因此他们垄断了这个特定的市场。

sentences.en: Just for those people who are wondering, we were talking about how glamorous Amsterdam is.
sentences.zh: 对于那些感到好奇的人，我们刚才还在讨论阿姆斯特丹是多么迷人。

sentences.en: And we are, Tom, you've picked a location that is right by the bins.
sentences.zh: 而我们现在，汤姆，你选了一个就在垃圾桶旁边的地点。

sentences.en: Yes.

sentences.zh: 所以，如果你自己来阿姆斯特丹旅行，除非你想重新体验一把完整的汤姆·霍兰德式旅程，否则我建议你不要去垃圾桶旁边。

sentences.en: Well, you know, we're going into the dark underbelly of Amsterdam as well as looking simply at the
sentences.zh: 好吧，你知道的，我们要探索阿姆斯特丹黑暗阴暗的一面，也要欣赏它的美丽之处。

sentences.en: I mean, that's very good.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那真的很好。

sentences.en: So we are now, we've come to the second location that I've chosen.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在，我们来到了我选的第二个地点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And you will see that it is the Amsterdam Dungeon.
sentences.zh: 你会看到那是阿姆斯特丹地牢。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Which I think is a franchise organized by the London Dungeon.
sentences.zh: 我想这是由伦敦地牢组织的一个连锁加盟店。

sentences.en: So it's kind of basically waxworks of people being tortured.
sentences.zh: 所以它基本上有点像是人们遭受酷刑的蜡像馆。

sentences.en: That kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事。

sentences.en: So you may think, well, why have I brought you here?
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会想，嗯，我为什么带你们来这里？

sentences.en: I actually genuinely enjoy those things, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我其实真的很喜欢这些东西，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, I'm going to ruin your sense of enjoyment now by saying that we have come here, not because
sentences.zh: 好吧，我现在要破坏你的乐趣了，我要说的是我们来到这里，不是因为

sentences.en: of the London Dungeon itself, but because of what stood here, which was a church, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 伦敦地牢本身，而是因为这里以前的东西，那是一座教堂，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So we were talking before about how it was that Amsterdam starts to emerge from just being a kind of collection of people camped out next to a bog going fishing for herring.
sentences.zh: 所以我们之前讨论过阿姆斯特丹是如何从一个仅仅是露营在沼泽旁捕捞鲱鱼的人群聚集地发展起来的。

sentences.en: There was an awful lot of herrings involved in that early sequence.
sentences.zh: 早期那段历史里涉及了大量的鲱鱼。

sentences.en: I mean, it's quite a rough place, but it's also pious, as you would expect for people kind of living very close to the elements.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那是个相当粗犷的地方，但正如你对那些在大自然边缘生活的人们所期望的那样，它也很虔诚。

sentences.en: So there's a definite sense, I think, which runs throughout the history of Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为，在阿姆斯特丹的整个历史中，有一种明确的意识贯穿始终。

sentences.en: Descartes, who came to stay here, kind of famously said that God made the world, but the Dutch made Holland.
sentences.zh: 曾经来这里小住的笛卡尔曾有句名言：上帝创造了世界，而荷兰人创造了荷兰。

sentences.en: And there is this sense that the ability to win land from the sea is a kind of marker of divine favor.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种感觉，即从海中赢得土地的能力是一种神圣恩宠的标志。

sentences.en: So Amsterdam, although it's rough, is a pretty pious place.
sentences.zh: 所以阿姆斯特丹虽然粗犷，却是一个相当虔诚的地方。

sentences.en: But what really turbo charges the sense of Amsterdam as a godly city in the Middle Ages is a spectacular
sentences.zh: 但真正让阿姆斯特丹在中世纪成为一座神圣城市的信念加速发展的，是一场壮观的

sentences.en: miracle, Dominic, which happened on the very spot where we are now, looking at the Amsterdam dungeon.
sentences.zh: 奇迹，多米尼克，它就发生在现在我们正看着阿姆斯特丹地牢的这个地方。

sentences.en: So this took place in 1345, and it was called The Miracle of Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 所以这发生在1345年，被称为阿姆斯特丹奇迹。

sentences.en: And it took place on Tuesday before Palm Sunday.
sentences.zh: 它发生在棕枝主日前的星期二。

sentences.en: So kind of the week before Holy Week.
sentences.zh: 也就是圣周前的那一周。

sentences.en: And there's an old man, and he's quietly dying in his house.
sentences.zh: 有一个老人，他正在自己的屋里静静地死去。

sentences.en: The priest comes, gives him final sacrament.
sentences.zh: 神父来了，给他做了临终圣事。

sentences.en: And he takes the consecrated bread on his tongue, and then he vomits, Dominic, and he pukes it up.
sentences.zh: 他把圣餐饼含在舌头上，然后他呕吐了，多米尼克，他吐了出来。

sentences.en: And the Holy Sacrament is in the puke.
sentences.zh: 而圣餐就在呕吐物里。

sentences.en: So difficult to know what to do.
sentences.zh: 所以很难知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: So they decide, well, we'll chuck it on the fire.
sentences.zh: 于是他们决定，好吧，我们把它扔进火里。

sentences.en: That's probably the best way to get rid of it.
sentences.zh: 这可能是摆脱它的最好方法。

sentences.en: And they chuck it on the fire, and it doesn't burn.
sentences.zh: 他们把它扔进火里，结果它没有烧毁。

sentences.en: And they try it again, and it still doesn't burn.
sentences.zh: 他们再试一次，它依然没有烧毁。

sentences.en: And so they clean it of the sick.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把上面的呕吐物清洗干净。

sentences.en: And they take it to the local priest, and he's amazed and thinks that this is highly supernatural.
sentences.zh: 他们把它带给当地的神父，神父大为惊奇，认为这是高度超自然的现象。

sentences.en: And they say that it's a miracle.
sentences.zh: 他们说这是一个奇迹。

sentences.en: And so they build a church around it, and then the church burns down, and still it doesn't burn.
sentences.zh: 于是他们围绕它建造了一座教堂，然后教堂被烧毁了，然而它仍然没有烧毁。

sentences.en: The sacrament still survives.
sentences.zh: 圣餐依然保存了下来。

sentences.en: And then the church burns down again, and still it doesn't burn down.
sentences.zh: 然后教堂再次被烧毁，然而它依然没有烧毁。

sentences.en: So this is an absolute proof that this is a spectacular miracle.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对证明了这是一个壮观的奇迹。

sentences.en: And so Amsterdam becomes a great, great center of pilgrimage.
sentences.zh: 因此阿姆斯特丹成为了一个伟大而又伟大的朝圣中心。

sentences.en: And actually, all the kind of streets around here, they're kind of holy road, holy place, all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这里周围所有的街道，它们就像是圣路、圣地，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So even though this is absolutely the heart of kind of the modern-day tourist heart of the city, there are trace elements of that.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管这里绝对是现代城市游客的核心地带，但仍有一些历史痕迹的元素。

sentences.en: So this is 14th, 15th century.
sentences.zh: 所以这是14、15世纪的事。

sentences.en: And this is absolutely not a question of a sort of herring fishing town in the middle of nowhere desperately needing to attract tourists.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不是一个荒郊野岭急需吸引游客的鲱鱼捕捞小镇的问题。

sentences.en: I think that would be an unduly cynical approach.
sentences.zh: 我认为那将是一种过度愤世嫉俗的方法。

sentences.en: No, because I don't think that you'd be getting, say, almost 100,000 people a year if it was a total fraud.
sentences.zh: 不，因为如果这是一个完全的骗局，我想你不会吸引到几乎每年将近10万人的到来。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: They'd all be coming here with their equivalent of their wise cards, ready to spend.
sentences.zh: 他们不会带着相当于他们智慧卡的装备来到这里，随时准备消费。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, some really very heavyweight figures came, including an emperor of, a future emperor of the Holy Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思，一些非常重量级的人物也曾造访，包括神圣罗马帝国的未来皇帝。

sentences.en: Oh, Maximilian.
sentences.zh: 哦，马克西米利安。

sentences.en: Maximilian in 1489.
sentences.zh: 马克西米利安在1489年。

sentences.en: So it's a very, very Catholic city.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常非常天主教的城市。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Great center of Catholic pilgrimage.
sentences.zh: 天主教朝圣的伟大中心。

sentences.en: And so that then focuses the question, how is it that this incredibly Catholic city comes to be one of the most famous centers of Protestantism?
sentences.zh: 那么这就引出了一个问题：这个极其天主教的城市怎么会成为新教最著名的中心之一呢？

sentences.en: Well, Tom, you mentioned Maximilian of Austria.
sentences.zh: 好吧，汤姆，你提到了奥地利的马克西米利安。

sentences.en: So at this point, there is no country called the Netherlands or Holland, is there?
sentences.zh: 所以在这一点上，还没有一个叫荷兰或尼德兰的国家，对吧？

sentences.en: This is part of the great Habsburg inheritance, right?
sentences.zh: 这是伟大的哈布斯堡遗产的一部分，对吧？

sentences.en: This is part of the great enormous Habsburg domain of the 16th century.
sentences.zh: 这是16世纪哈布斯堡庞大领地的一部分。

sentences.en: So Charles V, Philip II.
sentences.zh: 所以查理五世，腓力二世。

sentences.en: This is what used to be called the Spanish Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 这就是过去被称为西属尼德兰的地方。

sentences.en: Am I right?
sentences.zh: 我说的对吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So listeners may remember the episode we did with Bart van Loo on Burgundy.
sentences.zh: 所以听众们可能还记得我们和巴特·范·卢（Bart van Loo）关于勃艮第的那期节目。

sentences.en: And Burgundy and all that kind of conglomeration of the low countries, which includes what would today be Belgium, as well as the Netherlands, comes part of that inheritance.
sentences.zh: 勃艮第以及低地国家的所有这些联合体，其中包括今天的比利时以及荷兰，都成为了该遗产的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The thing about Amsterdam is that because it's on the periphery and because it's been won from the sea, its feudal obligations are unclear.
sentences.zh: 关于阿姆斯特丹的情况是，因为它地处边缘，而且是从海中赢得的土地，它的封建义务并不明确。

sentences.en: The Bishop of Utrecht, the local Lord of the Amstel, and the Count of Holland are all kind of fighting over it.
sentences.zh: 乌得勒支主教、阿姆斯特尔的当地领主以及荷兰伯爵都在争夺它。

sentences.en: And in the end, the Count of Holland kind of claims it.
sentences.zh: 最后，荷兰伯爵将其宣称为自己的领地。

sentences.en: But the city fathers are pretty independent.
sentences.zh: 但市议员们相当独立。

sentences.en: And so Charles V, who is having to deal with Luther, who's popped up by this stage, and so the Reformation is kicking off.
sentences.zh: 因此，查理五世不得不应付此时已经涌现的马丁·路德，宗教改革也由此拉开了序幕。

sentences.en: You know, he's saying to all the kind of the city authorities across the lowlands, stamp this out.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他对低地国家的各个城市当局说，把这个镇压下去。

sentences.en: But actually, the city fathers here in Amsterdam aren't keen on doing that.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，阿姆斯特丹的市议员并不热衷于这样做。

sentences.en: And basically, that's because it's a port.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这是因为它是一个港口。

sentences.en: It's an open city.
sentences.zh: 它是一个开放的城市。

sentences.en: It's always depended on welcoming people to come here.
sentences.zh: 它历来依靠欢迎人们来这里。

sentences.en: And they don't really want to kind of dig too deep.
sentences.zh: 他们其实不想深究此事。

sentences.en: And this will become very much a kind of Amsterdam tradition, that things that are on the cusp of legality, you kind of tolerate.
sentences.zh: 这将非常成为一种阿姆斯特丹传统，即处于合法性边缘的事情，你某种程度上会容忍。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because of the port, because of the sense of it being a melting pot, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想，因为港口的关系，因为这里是一个大熔炉的感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That if you're too top-down, you will squash the creativity and the free exchange on which
sentences.zh: 如果你采取过于自上而下的方式，你就会扼杀创造力和自由交流，而阿姆斯特丹

sentences.en: Amsterdam presumably depends.
sentences.zh: 想必正是依赖于这些。

sentences.en: And also the sense of a coherent civic culture.
sentences.zh: 还有一种连贯的公民文化意识。

sentences.en: Because without that, you can't keep the dams and the dikes and everything maintained and draining it of water.
sentences.zh: 因为没有这个，你就无法维持水坝、堤防以及一切设施并将其中的水排出。

sentences.en: So there isn't actually much persecution of the Protestants as they start to come here.
sentences.zh: 所以当新教徒开始来到这里时，实际上并没有受到太多的迫害。

sentences.en: There's one exception, which is the Anabaptists, who are very badly behaved at this stage.
sentences.zh: 有一个例外，那就是再洗礼派，他们在现阶段表现非常糟糕。

sentences.en: So famously, they take over Munster.
sentences.zh: 最著名的是，他们占领了明斯特。

sentences.en: And there's all kinds of carnage and horror there.
sentences.zh: 那里发生了一切血腥屠杀和恐怖事件。

sentences.en: There is an Anabaptist uprising here at the same time in 1535.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在1535年，这里也发生了一场再洗礼派起义。

sentences.en: And a load of Anabaptists take their clothes off and run around the town.
sentences.zh: 许多再洗礼派信徒脱掉衣服在镇上四处奔跑。

sentences.en: And they capture Dam Square, where we've just been.
sentences.zh: 他们占领了我们刚刚去过的水坝广场。

sentences.en: And they storm the city hall and they kill one of the city mayors.
sentences.zh: 他们冲进市政厅，杀死了一位市长。

sentences.en: So this doesn't go down well.
sentences.zh: 所以这并没有带来好结果。

sentences.en: And the Anabaptists, when this uprising gets suppressed, all get horribly killed.
sentences.zh: 当这场起义被镇压时，再洗礼派信徒们都遭到了可怕的杀害。

sentences.en: Their chests are cut open and their beating hearts are pulled out in front of them.
sentences.zh: 他们的胸膛被剖开，跳动的心脏在他们面前被掏出。

sentences.en: And they're drawn and quartered.
sentences.zh: 他们被施以车裂酷刑。

sentences.en: So Anabaptists are stamped on.
sentences.zh: 所以再洗礼派受到了严厉打压。

sentences.en: But the Calvinists, so the followers of Jean Calvin, who we talked about actually in our
sentences.zh: 但是加尔文派，也就是我们在我们的

sentences.en: Swiss episode, didn't we, in the World Cup.
sentences.zh: 瑞士那期世界杯节目中谈到的让·加尔文的追随者，不是吗？

sentences.en: They're much quieter.
sentences.zh: 他们安静得多。

sentences.en: They're much less prone to taking their clothes off and killing mares.
sentences.zh: 他们没那么容易脱衣服和杀害市长。

sentences.en: I see here from your notes, you've written the three words, much less barking.
sentences.zh: 我从你的笔记里看到，你写了三个字：没那么疯狂。

sentences.en: So that's bad news for our Anabaptist listeners.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我们的再洗礼派听众来说是个坏消息。

sentences.en: Well, the Anabaptists do kind of calm down.
sentences.zh: 好吧，再洗礼派确实平静了下来。

sentences.en: But by the standards of the mid-16th century, Calvinists are easier for the city fathers to tolerate.
sentences.zh: 但以16世纪中叶的标准来看，加尔文派更容易被市议员们所容忍。

sentences.en: And so basically, the city fathers in Amsterdam, it's still absolutely majority Catholic, but they're a kind of growing Calvinist population.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，阿姆斯特丹的市议员们，虽然这里绝大多数仍然是天主教徒，但有一个不断增长的加尔文派人口。

sentences.en: And they hope that they can kind of balance both sides.
sentences.zh: 他们希望自己能在某种程度上平衡双方。

sentences.en: However, events beyond Amsterdam's borders make that impossible.
sentences.zh: 然而，阿姆斯特丹边界之外的事件使这成为不可能。

sentences.en: Because in 1566, you have what, the Beeldensturm.
sentences.zh: 因为在1566年，发生了什么，圣像破坏运动（Beeldensturm）。

sentences.en: That's beautiful Dutch, Tom.
sentences.zh: 那是美丽的荷兰语，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well done.
sentences.zh: 干得好。

sentences.en: The kind of great fury of iconoclasm, which really kicks off in Antwerp, where there are a lot of Calvinists, far more Calvinists than in Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 那种巨大的破坏圣像狂热，实际上在安特卫普爆发了，那里有很多加尔文派，比阿姆斯特丹的加尔文派多得多。

sentences.en: And they go kind of berserk, ransacking everything, pulling down icons and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们变得有点疯狂，洗劫一切，推倒圣像等等。

sentences.en: And actually, in Ghent as well.
sentences.zh: 实际上，根特也是如此。

sentences.en: So again, we had, Bart was on our show, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以同样地，巴特曾做客我们的节目，对吧？

sentences.en: Talking about Belgium and the...
sentences.zh: 谈论比利时和……

sentences.en: And Jan van Eyck.
sentences.zh: 还有扬·凡·艾克。

sentences.en: Jan van Eyck.
sentences.zh: 扬·凡·艾克。

sentences.en: And that only gets saved because they hide it.
sentences.zh: 而那幅画之所以得救，是因为他们把它藏了起来。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The Ghent altarpiece.
sentences.zh: 根特祭坛画。

sentences.en: The Ghent altarpiece.
sentences.zh: 根特祭坛画。

sentences.en: In Amsterdam, it's less, again, it's less serious.
sentences.zh: 在阿姆斯特丹，情况没那么严重，同样也没那么严重。

sentences.en: So there's a woman who takes her slipper off and throws it at an icon of the Virgin.
sentences.zh: 所以有一个女人脱下她的拖鞋，扔向圣母的圣像。

sentences.en: Iconoclasts smash some stained glass.
sentences.zh: 圣像破坏者砸碎了一些彩色玻璃。

sentences.en: But again, the authorities in Amsterdam do not react to this with violent oppression.
sentences.zh: 但同样，阿姆斯特丹的当局并没有以暴力的压制来对此作出反应。

sentences.en: In fact, they do the opposite.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们做出了相反的举动。

sentences.en: They kind of try and negotiate with Calvinists and they say that they can hold services outside the city walls.
sentences.zh: 他们某种程度上试图与加尔文派谈判，并表示他们可以在城墙外举行礼拜。

sentences.en: And this is their approach to this kind of wave of iconoclasm.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们对待这种圣像破坏浪潮的方法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But this is not what the imperial authorities are allowing to happen.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是帝国当局允许发生的事情。

sentences.en: Because by now, Charles V has been succeeded by Philip II.
sentences.zh: 因为此时，查理五世已经由腓力二世继位。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Who, as English listeners will know, is the person who sends the Armada.
sentences.zh: 正如英国听众所知，他是派遣无敌舰队的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Very, very keen on stamping out Protestantism completely.
sentences.zh: 非常非常热衷于彻底根除新教。

sentences.en: And he basically orders a strategy of outright oppression.
sentences.zh: 他基本上命令采取全面压制的策略。

sentences.en: And this precipitates an enormous revolt from...
sentences.zh: 这引发了一场巨大的起义，从……

sentences.en: The famous Dutch revolt.
sentences.zh: 著名的尼德兰革命。

sentences.en: The famous Dutch revolt, which is initially focused in Southern Holland, but spreads northwards.
sentences.zh: 著名的尼德兰革命，最初集中在荷兰南部，但向北蔓延。

sentences.en: And Amsterdam, as this great center of Catholic pilgrimage, is really the kind of the holdout.
sentences.zh: 而阿姆斯特丹作为这个天主教朝圣的伟大中心，实际上是某种坚守阵地。

sentences.en: It doesn't side with this revolt.
sentences.zh: 它没有站在这场起义的一边。

sentences.en: So that by 1572, Amsterdam is pretty much the only city left in Spanish hands.
sentences.zh: 因此到1572年，阿姆斯特丹几乎成了唯一留在西班牙人手里的城市。

sentences.en: And so the Duke of Alba, who is the great, you know, the Iron Duke, this terrifying Spanish soldier, warlord, who is charged with the repression of the Dutch revolt.
sentences.zh: 所以阿尔巴公爵，也就是那个伟大的，你知道的，铁血公爵，那个可怕的西班牙士兵、军阀，负责镇压尼德兰革命的人。

sentences.en: He comes here and he makes Amsterdam his base.
sentences.zh: 他来到这里，把阿姆斯特丹作为他的基地。

sentences.en: And Catholic refugees from the kind of the rising tide of brought in success elsewhere in Holland, they kind of come here.
sentences.zh: 来自荷兰其他地方不断高涨的成功浪潮的天主教难民，他们来到了这里。

sentences.en: But also coming here are refugees from Antwerp.
sentences.zh: 但来到这里的还有来自安特卫普的难民。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Which has been sacked very, very brutally by the Spanish.
sentences.zh: 该城曾被西班牙人极其残酷地洗劫过。

sentences.en: So a lot of Calvinist refugees come here.
sentences.zh: 因此，大量加尔文教难民来到这里。

sentences.en: And by 1578, the city is, dare I say, a kindling box, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 到1578年，这座城市，请恕我直言，就像一个火药桶，多米尼克。

sentences.en: A tinderbox.
sentences.zh: 一个引火槽。

sentences.en: A tinderbox.
sentences.zh: 一个引火槽。

sentences.en: A tinderbox.
sentences.zh: 一个引火槽。

sentences.en: All it requires is the spark.
sentences.zh: 万事俱备，只欠东风。

sentences.en: So the spark comes on the 26th of May.
sentences.zh: 所以，星星之火在5月26日燃起。

sentences.en: But when it does come, what the Dutch call the alteration, which is a kind of wonderful euphemism.
sentences.zh: 但当它真的发生时，荷兰人称之为“变革”，这是一个相当美妙的委婉说法。

sentences.en: But it's not so much of a euphemism because it is actually a bloodless transfer of power from Catholics to Protestants.
sentences.zh: 但这与其说是委婉说法，不如说它实际上是权力从天主教徒向新教徒的和平过渡。

sentences.en: So all the Catholic members of the city council, again, so Dutch, they get put on barges.
sentences.zh: 因此，市议会中所有天主教成员，又很有荷兰特色地，被塞上了驳船。

sentences.en: They sail off and the Franciscans get kicked out.
sentences.zh: 他们扬帆远去，方济各会也被驱逐出境。

sentences.en: The monasteries and the convents get converted to other uses.
sentences.zh: 修道院和女修道院被改作他用。

sentences.en: So orphanages, prisons, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 比如孤儿院、监狱之类的地方。

sentences.en: The churches are whitewashed.
sentences.zh: 教堂被刷成了白色。

sentences.en: So it's a proper Protestant revolution.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一场名副其实的新教革命。

sentences.en: Yeah, it really is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And the oldest church in Amsterdam, it gets whitewashed and renamed the Oude Koerke, the old church.
sentences.zh: 阿姆斯特丹最古老的教堂被刷白，并更名为老教堂（Oude Koerke）。

sentences.en: And all the processions and ceremonies and commemorations of the miracle of Amsterdam are closed down.
sentences.zh: 所有关于阿姆斯特丹奇迹的游行、仪式和纪念活动都被叫停。

sentences.en: So the miracle church is transformed into a tourist trap.
sentences.zh: 于是，奇迹教堂变成了一个旅游陷阱。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so it's decreed that it will be turned into a center of waxworks.
sentences.zh: 因此当局下令将其改造成一个蜡像馆。

sentences.en: Very good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: And so this very, very Catholic city, pretty much overnight, has been rebranded as one of the strongholds of Protestantism and specifically Calvinism.
sentences.zh: 于是，这座原本非常非常天主教的城市，几乎在一夜之间被重新打造为新教、尤其是加尔文教的据点之一。

sentences.en: Then the question is, well, what happens to the surviving Catholics?
sentences.zh: 那么问题来了，幸存的天主教徒们怎么办？

sentences.en: Well, I bet you've got something up your sleeve, have you?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我敢说你早有准备，对吧？

sentences.en: I have.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We're going to go to a very quiet and peaceful location that will enable us to answer exactly that question.
sentences.zh: 我们要去一个非常安静祥和的地方，它能让我们完美回答这个问题。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的其余部分》。

sentences.en: We've come to this lovely oasis of calm in the center of Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 我们来到了阿姆斯特丹市中心这片宁静可爱的绿洲。

sentences.en: And Tom, explain to us where we are.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，给我们讲讲我们在哪儿。

sentences.en: We are in the Begeinhof.
sentences.zh: 我们在贝恩霍夫（Begeinhof）。

sentences.en: And so a hoffier is a courtyard with almshouses around it.
sentences.zh: 贝恩霍夫（hofier）是一个四周环绕着济贫院的庭院。

sentences.en: So this is the only medieval hoffier that has survived.
sentences.zh: 所以这是唯一幸存的中世纪贝恩霍夫。

sentences.en: So it dates back to the 14th century.
sentences.zh: 它的历史可以追溯到14世纪。

sentences.en: They're privately funded.
sentences.zh: 它们是私人出资兴建的。

sentences.en: They are veiled from the street.
sentences.zh: 它们与街道隔绝开来。

sentences.en: So to get in here, you've just come through a kind of a single door.
sentences.zh: 所以要进来，你刚才得穿过一扇很小的单门。

sentences.en: If anyone has been to a kind of Oxford or Cambridge college, it's that kind of vibe.
sentences.zh: 如果有人去过牛津或剑桥的学院，就会有那种氛围。

sentences.en: But privately funded and it's for charitable purposes.
sentences.zh: 但它是私人出资的，用于慈善目的。

sentences.en: So these are almshouses.
sentences.zh: 所以这些都是济贫院。

sentences.en: And then generally for women.
sentences.zh: 通常是为女性而设。

sentences.en: I mean, not always, but in this case, absolutely for women.
sentences.zh: 我是说，并不全是，但在这里，绝对是专门为女性准备的。

sentences.en: Because the Begeins are communities of lay women.
sentences.zh: 因为贝恩修女（Begeins）是由俗世女性组成的社群。

sentences.en: So they're not nuns.
sentences.zh: 所以她们不是修女。

sentences.en: They haven't kind of vowed chastity or poverty.
sentences.zh: 她们没有发誓过贞洁或贫困。

sentences.en: They swear themselves to virginity.
sentences.zh: 她们只发誓保持童贞。

sentences.en: And they're free to leave whenever they like.
sentences.zh: 而且她们随时可以离开。

sentences.en: So it's kind of Begein in French, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以在法语里有点像贝恩（Begein），对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: So these houses are sort of 17th century.
sentences.zh: 所以这些房子大约是17世纪的。

sentences.en: But that house there, the wooden house.
sentences.zh: 但那边那栋房子，那栋木屋。

sentences.en: Am I right in thinking that's the oldest house in the city?
sentences.zh: 我没记错的话，那是城里最古老的房子吧？

sentences.en: Yes, because there was a fire in 1521 and they introduced a ban on building wooden houses.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为1521年发生了一场火灾，他们随后颁布了禁止建造木屋的禁令。

sentences.en: So it must predate that.
sentences.zh: 所以它的建造时间肯定在那之前。

sentences.en: I think it's one of two wooden houses left in the city.
sentences.zh: 我想这是城里仅存的两栋木屋之一。

sentences.en: So yeah, so kind of fantastic relic.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这是一个非常了不起的遗迹。

sentences.en: But the reason for coming here isn't just that it's a famously beautiful spot, quiet spot.
sentences.zh: 但我们来这里的目的不仅因为它是一个著名的美丽静谧之地，

sentences.en: But that it focuses in on some of the kind of the paradoxes and tensions of the response of the Dutch,
sentences.zh: 还因为它集中体现了荷兰人的一些悖论和紧张关系，

sentences.en: and particularly of Amsterdamers, to what they call the alteration, the changeover from Catholic to Protestant.
sentences.zh: 尤其是阿姆斯特丹人对他们所谓的“变革”——从天主教向新教的转变——的反应。

sentences.en: So Catholic worship is banned.
sentences.zh: 因此，天主教崇拜被禁止了。

sentences.en: And so this is a problem for the Begeins, who are a Catholic order.
sentences.zh: 这对作为一个天主教修会的贝恩修女来说是个问题。

sentences.en: So we're sitting on a bench next to the church, which is 15th century.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正坐在一座15世纪教堂旁边的长椅上。

sentences.en: This gets taken from the Begeins and it stands empty for a couple of decades after the alteration.
sentences.zh: 这座教堂被从贝恩修女手中夺走，在“变革”之后的几十年里一直闲置。

sentences.en: And then in 1607, it's handed over to the English.
sentences.zh: 然后在1607年，它被移交给了英国人。

sentences.en: Oh, that's good.
sentences.zh: 哦，那挺好。

sentences.en: It's given to English-speaking Presbyterians.
sentences.zh: 它被交给了说英语的长老会教徒。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I mean, if you go inside, anyone who is familiar with 17th century churches in Britain would immediately recognize it's hung with English flags, Scottish flags, Union Jacks.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你走进去，任何熟悉英国17世纪教堂的人都会一眼认出里面挂满了英国国旗、苏格兰国旗和米字旗。

sentences.en: To this day, it remains aligned with the Church of Scotland, so the Presbyterians and the Church of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，它仍然与苏格兰教会保持一致，也就是长老会和苏格兰教会。

sentences.en: But the Begeins are not expelled.
sentences.zh: 但贝恩修女并没有被驱逐。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that the Amsterdamers have great respect for property law and the Begeins own all the houses.
sentences.zh: 原因在于阿姆斯特丹人非常尊重财产权，而且这些房子都是贝恩修女的私产。

sentences.en: So the church be confiscated, but not their houses.
sentences.zh: 所以教堂可以被没收，但她们的房子不行。

sentences.en: So the Hoffier remains their private property and they continue to be buried inside the church, even once the English Presbyterians have taken it over.
sentences.zh: 因此，这个贝恩霍夫依然是她们的私有财产，即使在英国长老会接管教堂之后，她们仍然继续被安葬在教堂内部。

sentences.en: And then in 1665, what they do is they take two of these private houses and they knock them together and they build a chapel.
sentences.zh: 然后在1665年，她们把两栋私有房屋打通，并在那里修建了一座小教堂。

sentences.en: And inside the chapel, they show a kind of wonderful artwork illustrating the miracle of Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 在小教堂里，她们展示了一件描绘阿姆斯特丹奇迹的精美艺术品。

sentences.en: So this great shrine that has been knocked down that we were just visiting.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们刚才参观的那座被砸毁的伟大神龛。

sentences.en: But I thought you said Catholicism was banned.
sentences.zh: 但你刚才不是说天主教被禁止了吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So this is, again, this distinctive Amsterdam approach to what is legal and what isn't.
sentences.zh: 所以这再次体现了阿姆斯特丹对于什么是合法、什么是不合法所持有的独特态度。

sentences.en: The Begeins approach the council and say, look, this is what we're doing.
sentences.zh: 贝恩修女找到议会说，听着，这就是我们要做的。

sentences.en: And the council's response is to say, OK, you can worship there, provided that it's hidden away, provided that it doesn't look like a chapel.
sentences.zh: 议会的反应则是，好吧，你们可以在那里做礼拜，前提是要隐蔽，前提是看起来不像一座小教堂。

sentences.en: So it has to continue looking like houses.
sentences.zh: 所以它必须继续看起来像普通的住宅。

sentences.en: So there's that sense in which they're simultaneously saying, yes, OK, it's legal, it's fine, go ahead with it, while at the same time saying, well, it isn't really.
sentences.zh: 因此，一方面他们似乎在说，行吧，这很合法，没问题，你们去做吧，但与此同时又在说，其实并非如此。

sentences.en: Oh, so this is what we're looking at.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以这就是我们现在看到的。

sentences.en: So this is what we're looking at now.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们现在看到的东西。

sentences.en: Because I was wondering, the stained glass windows in these, what appear to be these townhouses.
sentences.zh: 因为我一直在想，这些看起来像城市住宅的建筑上的彩色玻璃窗是怎么回事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that's actually a chapel.
sentences.zh: 那其实是一座小教堂。

sentences.en: And that is absolutely the chapel.
sentences.zh: 那绝对是一座小教堂。

sentences.en: And so this kind of provides a template for what is going on elsewhere in the city.
sentences.zh: 这为城里其他地方正在发生的事情提供了一种模版。

sentences.en: So actually, there's a Hofier built in 1614, which also serves as a refuge for Begeins.
sentences.zh: 事实上，1614年建造的另一个贝恩霍夫也同样充当了贝恩修女的避难所。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, there aren't chapels there, but Begeins settle there in Hofier.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那里虽然没有小教堂，但贝恩修女们在这个贝恩霍夫安顿了下来。

sentences.en: And also for kind of radical Protestant sects still.
sentences.zh: 同时也为一些激进的新教派别提供庇护。

sentences.en: So our friends, the Anabaptists, they're still lurking around.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的老朋友，再洗礼派教徒，依然潜伏在附近。

sentences.en: They're still around.
sentences.zh: 他们依然存在。

sentences.en: So they have their kind of their secret churches and their Hofiers.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有自己的秘密教堂和贝恩霍夫。

sentences.en: Mennonites, who are kind of another radical Protestant sect.
sentences.zh: 门诺会，这是另一个激进的新教派别。

sentences.en: But more generally, the Hofiers, these courtyards that are built with charitable intent.
sentences.zh: 但更广泛地说，这些带着慈善目的建造的庭院——贝恩霍夫。

sentences.en: This is a kind of impulse that survives the Reformation.
sentences.zh: 这是一种在宗教改革后存续下来的冲动。

sentences.en: So right the way up into the 19th century, there was famously a baron who got locked in his own strong room, counting his money.
sentences.zh: 因此，一直到19世纪，据说曾有一位男爵把自己反锁在金库里数钱，

sentences.en: And he made a vow that he would build a Hofier if he got out and didn't starve to death.
sentences.zh: 他发誓说，如果自己能活着出来而没被饿死，就要建一个贝恩霍夫。

sentences.en: And he did manage to get out.
sentences.zh: 结果他真的成功出来了。

sentences.en: So he built a Hofier.
sentences.zh: 于是他建了一个贝恩霍夫。

sentences.en: And if you come to Amsterdam and you want a kind of a way of getting to grips with the kind of the history and the character of the city, I think there is no better way than
sentences.zh: 如果你来到阿姆斯特丹，想要寻找一种方法来理解这座城市的历史和性格，我认为没有比这更好的方式了：

sentences.en: to do a tour of the Hofiers.
sentences.zh: 来一次贝恩霍夫巡游。

sentences.en: And you have to know where they are because they're often invisible.
sentences.zh: 而且你必须知道它们在哪儿，因为它们通常隐蔽无形。

sentences.en: They just look kind of little doorways, quiet doorways.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来只是小小的、宁静的门道。

sentences.en: So unless you know where you're going, you never know that there are these kind of incredible spaces hidden away from the street.
sentences.zh: 所以除非你知道自己要去哪儿，否则你永远不会知道街道深处还隐藏着这些不可思议的空间。

sentences.en: Because the point of the Hofiers is to be turned inwards, away from the street.
sentences.zh: 因为贝恩霍夫的设计理念就是向内看，背对街道。

sentences.en: So people can't see this, these terrible religious practices that you're getting up to and you're not infringing on the civic culture, which is overtly Protestant.
sentences.zh: 这样人们就看不到那些你们在进行的可怕宗教活动，而你们也没有触犯公开倡导新教的公民文化。

sentences.en: There is that, but there's also a kind of a value of inwardness, of privacy, a lack of public flourish that is expressive of the civic culture of the city, I think.
sentences.zh: 情况确实如此，但其中也蕴含着一种内敛、注重隐私、缺乏公开张扬的价值观，我认为这正是这座城市公民文化的体现。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This sense that the domestic is valuable and precious and something that is worth cultivating is absolutely a part of, I think, of what Amsterdam gives to the modern world.
sentences.zh: 这种认为家庭生活充满价值、珍贵且值得精心经营的观念，绝对是阿姆斯特丹对现代世界贡献的一部分。

sentences.en: You talked about this, didn't you, in the episode we did about the Dutch maid?
sentences.zh: 我们在制作关于荷兰女佣的那期节目里讨论过这个，对吧？

sentences.en: Remember the maid of Holland and the sort of the cleanliness, the domesticity, that's a very, very sort of golden age of the Dutch Republic kind of ethos, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 还记得荷兰女佣以及那种清洁感和家庭生活气息吗？这非常符合荷兰共和国黄金时代的精神风貌，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so we'll go and look at a particularly spectacular example of a Dutch townhouse in the second episode.
sentences.zh: 所以在第二集中，我们会去参观一个特别壮观的荷兰城市住宅范例。

sentences.en: But I think that these courtyards are, they're a very powerful, striking, and I think moving
sentences.zh: 但我认为这些庭院是一种非常有力、惊艳且动人的表达，

sentences.en: expression of that impulse towards valuing privacy and valuing the domestic, which is something I think, you know, pretty new by the standards of what had gone before.
sentences.zh: 展现了那种珍视隐私和家庭生活的冲动，按以往的标准来看，这在当时算得上相当新颖。

sentences.en: However, it would not at all do, Dominic, to imply that everyone in Amsterdam is going inwards
sentences.zh: 然而，多米尼克，如果暗示阿姆斯特丹的所有人都开始变得保守内向，那就大错特错了，

sentences.en: because 16th going into the 17th century, even as Hoffiers are being built and this sense of privacy is being valued.
sentences.zh: 因为随着16世纪迈入17世纪，即便贝恩霍夫在不断建造，这种隐私意识备受推崇的同时，

sentences.en: At the same time, Amsterdam is becoming the capital of globalisation.
sentences.zh: 阿姆斯特丹也在同步崛起为全球化之都。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, let's leave the Begeinhof behind and go and find your next location, which I think is a much more outward-looking one.
sentences.zh: 好了，让我们离开贝恩霍夫，去寻找你的下一个地点，我认为那是一个更加面向外部的地方。

sentences.en: It couldn't be more outward-looking, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 不可能再比那更面向外部了，多米尼克。

sentences.en: So, Tom, we've just walked down the street from the Begeinhof and we've come to another courtyard.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们刚刚从贝恩霍夫顺着街道走过来，来到了另一个庭院。

sentences.en: This is a courtyard of a very, very different-looking building, much grander, and this is the building
sentences.zh: 这是一个外观非常、非常不同的建筑的庭院，宏伟得多，正是这栋建筑

sentences.en: that tells us the story, doesn't it, of how Amsterdam goes from being basically a bit of a backwater to being the engine of globalisation.
sentences.zh: 向我们讲述了阿姆斯特丹如何从一个略显偏僻的边缘之地转变为全球化引擎的故事，对吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: So, in the 17th century, I mean, as you say, Amsterdam, an obscure backwater, a place that's
sentences.zh: 所以在17世纪，正如你所说，阿姆斯特丹曾是一个默默无闻的偏远角落，一个

sentences.en: still at war with the world's largest empire, but it becomes the birthplace of the modern, the modern world.
